title: Rav Chananyah, Brother’s Son of Rav Hoshayah
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: After much examination, Hyman suggests that his uncle Rav Hoshayah is the one called in the Jerusalem Talmud Rav Hoshayah, colleague of the Rabbis, brother of Rabbi Chananyah, colleague of the Rabbis, who were Rabbah’s brothers. He considers it impossible to say that this Rav Hoshaya refers to Rabbi Oshaya Rabbah, since Rabbi Oshayah’s place was in Tzippori and afterward in Caesarea, as explained in his entry, while this Rav Hoshaya’s place was in Tiberias, since they were before Rabbi Yochanan, who was head of the academy in Tiberias; as we find in Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 6:2: “The people of Tiberias say: from the great order up to the teaching of Rav Hoshaya.” In Jerusalem Talmud Taanit, chapter 1, end of halakhah 2: “Rabbi Yose (Rabbi Yonah’s colleague) said to Rabbi Chananyah [son of — so it is in Megillah 3:7] the brother of Rav Hoshaya: Do you remember when we were standing before the teaching of Rav Hoshayah, your uncle? Rabbi Ze’irah (I) passed by and we asked him, and he said: This is still a question for me. Rabbi Yasa passed by and we asked him.” Hyman regards the Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 3:7 text as corrupted, lacking there the name of the one who spoke to Rabbi Chananyah, and also it said there that Rabbi Ba bar Zavda passed and they asked him, and he said in Rav’s name. The precious book Mavo HaYerushalmi says that it is a scribal error and should read Ba bar Bizna; for in truth it is very far-fetched to say that Rabbi Abba bar Zavda, who was Rabbi Chanina bar Chama’s student, would live also after Rabbi Oshaya, the colleague of the Rabbis.

In Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat, beginning of halakhah 2 of chapter 1: “Rabbi Chananyah, brother’s son of Rav Hoshaya, says: Our Mishnah concerns the householder,” etc. Hyman suggests that possibly his father was Rabbi Shmuel, the brother of Rabbi Hoshaya, mentioned in Jerusalem Talmud Chagigah 2:7.

notes.text: חביבך is your uncle, consistent with the heading’s brother’s son. Hyman supplies תנותיה, rendered teaching; saved Guggenheimer Taanit1:2 instead has חנותיה and its English translates store, not teaching-house. His Megillah insertion of son of, distinction among the Hoshayah figures and Ba barZavda/Bizna proposal remain attributed. עוד אנא היא צריכה לי means the question is still unresolved for me, not a request for something needed.

The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 1:2 has chanuteh, store, where Hyman supplies tanuteh, teaching. Both are disclosed without silently replacing the supplied body. Uncle agrees with the heading’s brother’s son, and the answer leaves the question unresolved. Hyman’s distinctions among Hoshayah figures, Tiberias chronology, Ba bar Zavda/Bizna emendation and possible Shmuel parentage remain attributed.
